item.title: Internal Membranes Separate and Support Cellular Reactions
item.stimulus:
Liver cells make a molecule, Q, in the cytosol. The reactions that break Q down occur only inside a membrane-bound organelle, compartment K. Researchers prepared two extracts from the same liver tissue and supplied each with the raw materials needed to make Q.

Extract 1: cells were broken open gently, so the organelles, including compartment K, stayed intact.
Extract 2: cells were broken open harshly, so organelle membranes ruptured and the contents of compartment K mixed with the cytosol.

Table 1: Amount of Q present (μmol per gram of tissue)
Time (min) | Extract 1 | Extract 2
0 | 0 | 0
10 | 4.0 | 0.6
20 | 8.1 | 1.0
30 | 12.0 | 1.5

In a second study, the researchers compared two cell types in which reaction R is carried out by proteins embedded in internal membranes.

Table 2
Cell type | Internal membrane surface area per cell (μm²) | Rate of reaction R (relative units)
M | 1,500 | 30
N | 4,500 | 90

parts.prompt: Calculate the percent decrease in the amount of Q present at 30 minutes in Extract 2 compared with Extract 1.

criteria.text: Calculates a percent decrease of 87.5%: (12.0 − 1.5) ÷ 12.0 × 100 = 87.5%.
criteria.evidence: Response shows the difference (10.5 μmol per gram) divided by the Extract 1 value (12.0) and expresses the result as 87.5%, or uses an equivalent valid method such as (1 − 1.5/12.0) × 100.
criteria.fix: For percent decrease, divide the drop by the original (reference) value, then multiply by 100.

parts.prompt: Using the data in Table 1, explain how the membrane of compartment K allows Q to accumulate in Extract 1, and why much less Q accumulated in Extract 2.

criteria.text: Explains that the membrane of compartment K keeps the reactions that break down Q separate from the cytosol where Q is made, minimizing competing reactions; when the membrane ruptures (Extract 2), breakdown occurs in the same space as synthesis, so Q is broken down as it is made and only 1.5 μmol per gram accumulates versus 12.0.
criteria.evidence: Response links the intact membrane to separation of the competing synthesis and breakdown reactions, and links rupture to Q being broken down in the mixed extract, citing the lower amount of Q.
criteria.fix: Name the two opposing processes, state where each happens, and explain that the membrane keeps them apart so they cannot compete.

parts.prompt: Describe the relationship between internal membrane surface area and the rate of reaction R shown in Table 2.

criteria.text: Describes that the rate of reaction R increases as internal membrane surface area increases, in proportion: tripling the area (1,500 to 4,500 μm²) triples the rate (30 to 90).
criteria.evidence: Response states that greater internal membrane surface area is associated with a higher rate of reaction R, and notes the threefold change in both.
criteria.fix: Describe the direction of the trend and its size: compare how many times each variable changed between the two cell types.

parts.prompt: Explain how a larger area of internal membranes leads to the higher rate of reaction R in cell type N.

criteria.text: Explains that internal membranes increase the surface area where membrane-associated reactions can occur, providing room for more of the embedded proteins that carry out reaction R, so more reaction R can happen at the same time.
criteria.evidence: Response states that more internal membrane provides more surface area on which reaction R can take place (more embedded proteins), increasing the rate.
criteria.fix: Connect membrane area to reaction sites: more membrane surface holds more embedded proteins, so more reactions run at once.

item.model_answer:
(a) Percent decrease = (12.0 − 1.5) ÷ 12.0 × 100 = 10.5 ÷ 12.0 × 100 = 87.5%.

(b) In Extract 1, compartment K is intact, so its membrane keeps the reactions that break down Q inside the compartment, separate from the cytosol where Q is made. Because the opposing reactions are kept apart, they do not compete, and Q builds up steadily, reaching 12.0 μmol per gram at 30 minutes. In Extract 2, the ruptured membrane lets the contents of compartment K mix with the cytosol, so Q is broken down in the same space where it is being made. Much of the Q is broken down as soon as it forms, so only 1.5 μmol per gram accumulates.

(c) The rate of reaction R increases as internal membrane surface area increases. Cell type N has 3 times the internal membrane surface area of M (4,500 versus 1,500 μm²) and 3 times the rate (90 versus 30), so the rate rises in proportion to the membrane area.

(d) Reaction R is carried out by proteins embedded in internal membranes, so the reaction can occur only on membrane surfaces. A larger area of internal membrane increases the surface area where the reaction can occur and holds more of the embedded proteins, so more reaction R takes place at the same time and the rate is higher.

item.title: Lysosome Membrane Integrity and Mitochondrial Membrane Folding
item.stimulus:
Researchers studying compartmentalization in eukaryotic cells isolated lysosomes from liver cells. A lysosome is a membrane-bound sac containing hydrolytic enzymes.

The lysosomes were suspended in a buffered solution containing a substrate that the enzymes can break down. The substrate cannot cross an intact lysosomal membrane. Enzyme activity was measured in two samples:
- Sample 1: lysosomes left intact.
- Sample 2: lysosomes treated with a detergent that dissolves membranes.

Assume that the detergent exposes all of the lysosomal enzyme to the substrate and does not change enzyme activity.

Treatment | Enzyme activity detected (units)
Intact lysosomes | 12
Detergent-treated lysosomes | 96

In a separate part of the study, the researchers compared mitochondria from two cell types. Mitochondria in heart muscle cells have many more inner-membrane folds than mitochondria in liver cells.
item.model_answer:
(a) The lysosomal membrane surrounds the hydrolytic enzymes and keeps them separate from the cytosol and from the rest of the cell's molecules. Because of this, the hydrolysis reactions happen only inside the lysosome.

(b) The detergent exposes all of the enzyme, so 96 units is the total activity. Percentage detected with intact lysosomes = (12 ÷ 96) × 100 = 12.5%.

(c) I predict that the released hydrolytic enzymes will break down the cell's own proteins, nucleic acids and other macromolecules, damaging the cell and possibly killing it. Normally the lysosomal membrane keeps these enzymes apart from cytosolic molecules. Once the membrane ruptures, the enzymes are no longer compartmentalized and can reach substrates they normally never contact. The data support this: removing the membrane with detergent raised the detected activity from 12 to 96 units.

(d) The inner mitochondrial membrane is where the ATP-producing reactions of aerobic respiration take place. More folds give the membrane more surface area, so more of these reactions can occur at once. Heart mitochondria can therefore make more ATP, which matches the high, continuous energy demand of heart muscle.

item.title: Mitochondrial Inner Membrane Folding and Lysosome Containment
item.stimulus:
Researchers isolated mitochondria from two types of animal cells: heart muscle cells and liver cells. The mitochondria from both cell types were of similar overall size. The researchers measured the surface area of the outer and inner mitochondrial membranes. They supplied each sample with excess substrate and oxygen, then measured the relative rate of ATP synthesis per mitochondrion. Mean results are shown below.

Source of mitochondria | Outer membrane area (µm²) | Inner membrane area (µm²) | Relative ATP synthesis rate (arbitrary units)
Heart muscle cell | 6.0 | 30.0 | 120
Liver cell | 6.0 | 15.0 | 60

In a separate experiment, the researchers treated cultured liver cells with a drug that makes lysosomal membranes leaky, so that the contents of lysosomes escape into the cytosol.
item.model_answer:
(a) Heart muscle: 30.0 µm² ÷ 6.0 µm² = 5.0. Liver: 15.0 µm² ÷ 6.0 µm² = 2.5. Heart mitochondria have an inner to outer membrane area ratio of 5.0, and liver mitochondria have a ratio of 2.5.

(b) There is a positive, proportional relationship. Heart mitochondria have twice the inner membrane area of liver mitochondria (30.0 vs 15.0 µm²) and twice the ATP synthesis rate (120 vs 60). The rate per µm² of inner membrane is the same in both: 120 ÷ 30.0 = 4 and 60 ÷ 15.0 = 4.

(c) The inner membrane is folded, which greatly increases its surface area without increasing the size of the mitochondrion. The reactions that synthesize ATP occur on the inner membrane, so more membrane surface provides more sites for these reactions, allowing the mitochondrion to produce more ATP.

(d) The cells will be damaged and are likely to die, because the hydrolytic enzymes released from lysosomes will break down the cell's own proteins, membranes and organelles. Normally the lysosomal membrane compartmentalizes these hydrolytic enzymes, keeping digestion inside the lysosome and separate from the cytosol. This separation minimizes competing interactions between digestive reactions and the rest of the cell's processes. When the membrane leaks, that separation is lost.

item.title: Lysosomal Compartmentalization and Enzyme pH Dependence
item.stimulus:
Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles containing hydrolytic enzymes. The lysosomal membrane contains ATP-driven proton pumps that move H⁺ ions from the cytosol into the lysosome, keeping the lysosomal interior at about pH 4.8, while the surrounding cytosol is at about pH 7.2. A researcher purified two enzymes from liver cells: a lysosomal protease (enzyme L) and a cytosolic enzyme that participates in a metabolic pathway in the cytosol (enzyme C). The activity of each enzyme was measured in buffers at three pH values under otherwise identical conditions.

Enzyme activity (nmol product formed per minute per mg enzyme)
pH | Enzyme L (lysosomal protease) | Enzyme C (cytosolic enzyme)
4.8 | 84 | 7
6.0 | 38 | 31
7.2 | 5 | 66
item.model_answer:
(a) Enzyme L is a hydrolytic enzyme that breaks down proteins. Because it is enclosed inside the lysosomal membrane, it is physically separated from the cytosol, so it cannot reach and hydrolyze the cell's own cytosolic proteins and other macromolecules. Digestion is confined to material inside the lysosome.

(b) Percent decrease = (84 − 5) / 84 × 100 = 79 / 84 × 100 ≈ 94.0%.

(c) The breakdown of proteins inside the lysosomes will decrease greatly. The proton pumps normally use ATP to move H⁺ into the lysosome, keeping it at pH 4.8. With the pumps blocked, the lumen rises to pH 7.2. The data show enzyme L activity falls from 84 to 5 nmol/min/mg at pH 7.2, a decrease of about 94%, so very little protein will be hydrolyzed.

(d) The lysosomal membrane keeps two different environments in one cell: an acidic interior near pH 4.8 and a neutral cytosol near pH 7.2. Enzyme L has its highest activity at pH 4.8 (84) and enzyme C has its highest activity at pH 7.2 (66). If both were in a single compartment at one pH, one enzyme would work poorly (enzyme C has only 7 at pH 4.8, and enzyme L has only 5 at pH 7.2). Compartmentalization minimizes these competing requirements, so each enzyme operates near its optimum at the same time.

item.title: Membrane Compartments in Mitochondria and Lysosomes
item.stimulus:
Eukaryotic cells contain internal membranes that divide the cell into specialized compartments. A group of researchers isolated mitochondria from two cell types, X and Y, taken from the same animal. For a typical mitochondrion from each cell type, they measured the surface area of the outer mitochondrial membrane and the surface area of the folded inner mitochondrial membrane. They also measured the rate of ATP synthesis per mitochondrion under identical conditions. The results are shown below.

Cell type | Outer membrane area (µm²) | Inner membrane area (µm²) | ATP synthesis rate (arbitrary units per mitochondrion)
X | 6 | 30 | 100
Y | 6 | 12 | 40

In a separate experiment, the researchers treated cultured cells with a compound that makes lysosomal membranes leaky. The lysosomes remain present, but their contents can escape into the cytosol.
item.model_answer:
(a) Cell type X: 30 µm² / 6 µm² = 5. Cell type Y: 12 µm² / 6 µm² = 2. The inner-to-outer membrane ratio is 5 for X and 2 for Y.

(b) The inner membrane of a mitochondrion from X has 30 µm² of surface area compared with 12 µm² in Y, which is 2.5 times as much. The ATP synthesis rate in X (100) is also 2.5 times the rate in Y (40). The folded inner membrane is where the membrane-embedded proteins that carry out ATP synthesis are located, so a more highly folded inner membrane provides more surface area and more sites for these reactions to occur at the same time. This allows mitochondria from X to synthesize ATP faster than those from Y.

(c) I predict that proteins and other macromolecules, and even organelles, in the cytosol will be broken down or damaged, which will impair cell function and may kill the cell. Lysosomes contain hydrolytic enzymes that digest macromolecules. The lysosomal membrane normally compartmentalizes these enzymes, keeping them separate from the cytosol so that they do not interact with the cell's own molecules. When the membrane becomes leaky, this separation is lost, so the hydrolytic enzymes can reach and hydrolyze cytosolic components.

item.title: Lysosomal Enzyme pH and Membrane Compartmentalization
item.stimulus:
Lysosomes are membrane-bound organelles that contain hydrolytic enzymes. Proton pumps in the lysosomal membrane use ATP to move H⁺ ions from the cytosol into the lysosome. This keeps the lysosome interior near pH 4.8, while the surrounding cytosol is near pH 7.2.

Researchers purified one lysosomal enzyme that hydrolyzes proteins. They measured its activity in buffered solutions at different pH values, keeping temperature, enzyme concentration, and substrate concentration the same. The results are shown below.

pH | Enzyme activity (nmol of substrate hydrolyzed per minute per mg enzyme)
4.0 | 70
4.8 | 96
5.6 | 58
6.4 | 21
7.2 | 6
item.model_answer:
(a) The lysosomal membrane keeps the hydrolytic enzymes separate from the cytosol. Digestion therefore happens only inside the lysosome, and the enzymes do not hydrolyze the cell's own proteins and other macromolecules. This compartmentalization minimizes competing or harmful interactions with other cellular processes.

(b) Percent decrease = (96 − 6) ÷ 96 × 100 = 90 ÷ 96 × 100 = 93.75%, or about 94%.

(c) The released enzyme will hydrolyze cytosolic proteins at a low rate. At the cytosolic pH of 7.2, the enzyme's activity is only 6 nmol/min per mg, compared with 96 at the lysosomal pH of 4.8. That is only about 6% of its activity inside the lysosome. The neutral pH of the cytosol greatly reduces the enzyme's activity, so the few released enzymes cause little damage.

(d) Protein digestion inside the lysosome will decrease. The proton pumps use ATP to actively transport H⁺ into the lysosome, which keeps the interior near pH 4.8. If the pumps are blocked, H⁺ is no longer pumped in, and the lysosome interior becomes less acidic, with its pH rising toward the cytosolic pH. The data show that the enzyme's activity falls sharply as pH rises above 4.8, for example to 21 at pH 6.4 and 6 at pH 7.2. As a result, the enzymes hydrolyze proteins more slowly.

item.title: Mitochondrial Membrane Folding and Lysosome Compartments
item.stimulus:
A cell biologist uses electron microscopy to compare mitochondria from two types of mammalian cells: liver cells and heart muscle cells. Heart muscle cells contract continuously and have a very high demand for ATP. For a typical mitochondrion of each cell type, the biologist estimates the surface area of the outer mitochondrial membrane and of the folded inner mitochondrial membrane. The results are shown below.

Cell type | Outer membrane area per mitochondrion (µm²) | Inner membrane area per mitochondrion (µm²)
Liver | 12 | 36
Heart muscle | 12 | 120

In a separate experiment, the biologist treats cultured liver cells with a chemical that makes lysosomal membranes break open. This releases the lysosome's hydrolytic enzymes into the cytosol. The chemical has no other direct effects on the cell.
item.model_answer:
(a) Ratio = inner membrane area ÷ outer membrane area = 120 µm² ÷ 12 µm² = 10. The inner membrane has 10 times the area of the outer membrane, a 10:1 ratio.

(b) The heart muscle mitochondrion has 120 µm² of inner membrane, compared with 36 µm² in the liver mitochondrion. That is about 3.3 times as much, even though the outer membranes are the same size. The inner membrane is where the reactions and proteins that synthesize ATP are located. Its greater folding gives heart mitochondria more surface area where these reactions can occur. As a result, each heart mitochondrion can produce more ATP. This meets the high, continuous energy demand of contracting heart muscle cells.

(c) The proteins and other macromolecules in the cytosol will be hydrolyzed, or digested. Organelles may also be damaged, so the cells will be harmed and are likely to die. Normally the lysosomal membrane compartmentalizes the hydrolytic enzymes and keeps them separated from the rest of the cell. This minimizes competing and harmful interactions between the enzymes and the cell's own molecules. When the membrane breaks open, the enzymes reach cytosolic macromolecules they could not contact before, and they break them down.

item.title: Internal Membranes Separate and Support Cellular Reactions
item.stimulus:
Liver cells make a molecule, Q, in the cytosol. The reactions that break Q down occur only inside a membrane-bound organelle, compartment K. Researchers prepared two extracts from the same liver tissue and supplied each with the raw materials needed to make Q.

Extract 1: cells were broken open gently, so the organelles, including compartment K, stayed intact.
Extract 2: cells were broken open harshly, so organelle membranes ruptured and the contents of compartment K mixed with the cytosol.

Table 1: Amount of Q present (μmol per gram of tissue)
Time (min) | Extract 1 | Extract 2
0 | 0 | 0
10 | 4.0 | 0.6
20 | 8.1 | 1.0
30 | 12.0 | 1.5

In a second study, the researchers compared two cell types in which reaction R is carried out by proteins embedded in internal membranes.

Table 2
Cell type | Internal membrane surface area per cell (μm²) | Rate of reaction R (relative units)
M | 1,500 | 30
N | 4,500 | 90

parts.prompt: Calculate the percent decrease in the amount of Q present at 30 minutes in Extract 2 compared with Extract 1.

criteria.text: Calculates a percent decrease of 87.5%: (12.0 − 1.5) ÷ 12.0 × 100 = 87.5%.
criteria.evidence: Response shows the difference (10.5 μmol per gram) divided by the Extract 1 value (12.0) and expresses the result as 87.5%, or uses an equivalent valid method such as (1 − 1.5/12.0) × 100.
criteria.fix: For percent decrease, divide the drop by the original (reference) value, then multiply by 100.

parts.prompt: Using the data in Table 1, explain how the membrane of compartment K allows Q to accumulate in Extract 1, and why much less Q accumulated in Extract 2.

criteria.text: Explains that the membrane of compartment K keeps the reactions that break down Q separate from the cytosol where Q is made, minimizing competing reactions; when the membrane ruptures (Extract 2), breakdown occurs in the same space as synthesis, so Q is broken down as it is made and only 1.5 μmol per gram accumulates versus 12.0.
criteria.evidence: Response links the intact membrane to separation of the competing synthesis and breakdown reactions, and links rupture to Q being broken down in the mixed extract, citing the lower amount of Q.
criteria.fix: Name the two opposing processes, state where each happens, and explain that the membrane keeps them apart so they cannot compete.

parts.prompt: Describe the relationship between internal membrane surface area and the rate of reaction R shown in Table 2.

criteria.text: Describes that the rate of reaction R increases as internal membrane surface area increases, in proportion: tripling the area (1,500 to 4,500 μm²) triples the rate (30 to 90).
criteria.evidence: Response states that greater internal membrane surface area is associated with a higher rate of reaction R, and notes the threefold change in both.
criteria.fix: Describe the direction of the trend and its size: compare how many times each variable changed between the two cell types.

parts.prompt: Explain how a larger area of internal membranes leads to the higher rate of reaction R in cell type N.

criteria.text: Explains that internal membranes increase the surface area where membrane-associated reactions can occur, providing room for more of the embedded proteins that carry out reaction R, so more reaction R can happen at the same time.
criteria.evidence: Response states that more internal membrane provides more surface area on which reaction R can take place (more embedded proteins), increasing the rate.
criteria.fix: Connect membrane area to reaction sites: more membrane surface holds more embedded proteins, so more reactions run at once.

item.model_answer:
(a) Percent decrease = (12.0 − 1.5) ÷ 12.0 × 100 = 10.5 ÷ 12.0 × 100 = 87.5%.

(b) In Extract 1, compartment K is intact, so its membrane keeps the reactions that break down Q inside the compartment, separate from the cytosol where Q is made. Because the opposing reactions are kept apart, they do not compete, and Q builds up steadily, reaching 12.0 μmol per gram at 30 minutes. In Extract 2, the ruptured membrane lets the contents of compartment K mix with the cytosol, so Q is broken down in the same space where it is being made. Much of the Q is broken down as soon as it forms, so only 1.5 μmol per gram accumulates.

(c) The rate of reaction R increases as internal membrane surface area increases. Cell type N has 3 times the internal membrane surface area of M (4,500 versus 1,500 μm²) and 3 times the rate (90 versus 30), so the rate rises in proportion to the membrane area.

(d) Reaction R is carried out by proteins embedded in internal membranes, so the reaction can occur only on membrane surfaces. A larger area of internal membrane increases the surface area where the reaction can occur and holds more of the embedded proteins, so more reaction R takes place at the same time and the rate is higher.
